full_judgment:
5. Plaintiff's case in short is that on January 29, 1971 at 18-30 hours P.T. "BIRAL" a tug boat of plaintiff left Narayanganj for Chalna Port via Madhumati along with Barge No. PRS-536 and Barge No.PRS-553 on its starboard side; and Barge No. PRS-539 and Barge No. PRS-535 on its portside All the four barges were loaded with cargoes of gunny bales, rolls of carpet backing and bagging cloths. Barge No. 536 was carrying 479 bales of gunnies and 30 rolls of carpet backing weighing approximately 5390 maunds, under Invoice No. 697 of 2. 2.197 I for 300 bales of hessian tarpuling cloth and Invoice No. 698 of 2. 2.1971 for 179 bales of hessian tarpuling cloth and Invoice No. 699 of 3.2.1971 for 30 rolls carpet backing, consigned by Latif Bawany Jute Mills Ltd; and that Barge No. 553 was carrying 370 pales of gunnies weighing approximately 4977 maunds 30 seers, under Invoice No. 677 of 29.1.1971 for 306 bales of Cotton bagging cloth and Invoice No. 678 of 29.1.1971 for 64 bales of Cotton bagging cloth, consigned by the Fabric Ltd. In the both the consignments the consignors were the consignees. That all the holds of all the barges were sounded regularly during the voyage and found dry; and that the barges were in all respects sound, sea-worthy and well-equipped before they were loaded with cargo at Narayanganj and they were so all along. The tug boat P. T. Biral was in all respects sound, sea-worthy and properly equipped for voyage and to-wage. On January, 30, 1971 after mid-night, Muzaffar Ahmed (No. 1146) Second Master of P. T. BIRAL took over duty from the First Master Mozammel. Haque (No. 1274) while the flotilla was near Dood Mukhi point in the Sundarbans On January 31, 1971 at about 04:15 hours while the flotilla was approaching the mouth of Champai river the Second Master Muzaffar Ahmed gave repeated warning blats on the whistle to warn any approaching vessel on the main-river Pussur running North to South. The Second Master did neither hear any answering blast of any approaching vessel nor did he see the navigation light or search light of any vessel on the Pussurriver. On entering the Passur river from the eastern side and while turning right towards Chalna, the Second Master suddenly observed the red and white mast light of an approaching deep sea vessel approaching from North to South, that is, from the direction of the Chalna Port. When the ship was first sighted it was at a long distance from the flotilla. In order to give the deep sea vessel a clear passage the Second Master gave a short blast on the whistle and altered course to star board side. Then with the aid of his engines he turned the flotilla around and stemmed the tide. Thereafter he gave two short blast on the whistle and moved close to the eastern bank as far as possible. At this time the distance between the bank and the barge at the extreme port side was about 15½ only. The flotilla by this time was almost in a stationary position. About 2½ minutes after the Second Master completely turned round the flotilla, the afore said deep sea vessel which was m. v. HELLENIC PIONEER came with full speed and struck with her stem the star board side of Barge No.PRS-553 at a point close to the crew's accommodation. The time of impact was about 04:30 hours. As a result of this violent dash by the m. v. HELLENIC PIONEER, Barge No. PRS-553 sank on the spot instantaneously with all cargo on board and her crew were thrown into the river. Barge No. PRS-536 wail also heavily damaged and started taking water into its holds. The crew of Barge No.PRS-553, namely, Julfiquer (No. 2217) Serang, Abdul Mannan (No. 7384) Laskar and Abul Kalam another Laskar received serious injuries on their persons; and another Laskar Habibur Rahman (No. 6109) could not be traced in spite of all efforts and is presumed to be dead. The crew of Barge No. PRS-536, namely, Eskander Ali (No. 2253) Serang and Dana Mia (No. 4216) Laskar also received injuries due to the impact. The Second Master on seeing the crew of Barge No. PRS-553 in water immediately maneuvered the tug close to them for their rescue and when his attention was drawn by the crew of Barge No. PRS-536 that the said barge was sinking, he immediately made fast the barge on the port side of the tug in an effort to beaching her on river Champai. But before the barge could be beached she sank with all the cargo on board. The Second Master of P. T. BIRAL did all that was practicable for him to avoid the collision. At the time of collision the flotilla was almost in a stationary position keeping the fair navigation passage clear for the ship. The collision was due to sheer negligence and carelessness on the part of the Master and Crew of m.v. HELLENIC PIONEER, and as they are fully responsible for the loss of the Barges PRS-553 and PRS- 536 as also the cargo they were carrying; and further for loss of life of Laskar Habibur Rahman; for injuries inflicted on the crew Julfiquer, Abdul Mannan, Abu I Kalam, Eskandar Ali and Dana Mia. There was absolutely no negligence on the part of Master and Second Master of P. T. BJRAL has also of the Serangs and crew of the Barges which were being towed at the time. That the deep sea vessel m. v.  HELENIC PIONEER did not care to stop after the collision and proceeded on her voyage. P. T. BIRAL after rescue operations and connecting the remaining barges proceeded to Chalna and reported the matter to the relevant authorities. The m. v. HELLENIC PIONEER was recalled by the Port Authorities and she was back to Chalna Port on the morning of February 1, 1971. On January 31,1971 Muzaffar Ahmed (No. 1146) Second Master of P. T. BIRAL, Eskandar Ali (No. 2253) Serang of Barge No. PRS-536 and Zulfiquer (No. 2217) Serang of Barge No.PRS-553 lodged an Ejhar reporting the above facts of the collision before the Chalna Port Police Authorities. The Second Master, Muzaffar Ahmed lodged another ejhar on February 5, 1971 reporting the fact of non-traceability of Laskar Habibur Rahman and apprehending his death on February 5, 1971 Protest Affidavits concerning the fact of collision were sworn by Serang Eskander Ali and Serang Zulfiquer and on February 10, 1971 by the Second Master, Muzaffar Ahmed before the Magistrate, 1st Class, Khulna. On February I, 1971 proforma defendant No. 4 issued a claim notice on the plaintiff against complete loss of 3.70 bales of Cotton Bagging due to sinking of Barge No. PRS-553 Further in continuation of their above noted claim notice the said proforma defendant No. 4 on February 12, 1971 issued another notice on the plaintiff holding them responsible for the loss of the cargo, described as above, worth Rs. 3,34,596.00 Plaintiff by letters dated February 2, 1971 and February 16, 1971 addressed to the defendant No. repudiated fully their liability for the aforesaid loss of cotton bagging on the ground that the collision was caused due to carelessness, negligence and misconduct on the part of the Master and Crew of the m. v. HELLENIC PIONEER. Plaintiff's Agent at Khulna issued a notice of claim dated February 2, 1971 on the defendant No. 1 HELLENIC LINES LTD. with copies to defendant No.2 the local agents of defendant No. 1 and other relevant authorities for compensation for the loss of the above noted Barges along with cargoes. Plaintiff repudiated the claims of Fabrics Ltd. and Latif Bawany Jute Mills Ltd. for the loss of their goods on the plea that the liability laid entirely on the Master and Crew of m. v. HELLENIC PIONEER. In this context, the plaintiff further stated that inspite of best efforts neither the cargoes nor the sunken barges could be salvaged. Plaintiff approached the Pakistan Salvage Corporation Ltd. but the latter declined to undertake the salvage operation having regard to the depth of water at the site and consequent hazards and un-certainties. Ultimately the barges were declared as wreck by the plaintiff.
